observation.visible_scene: A high-speed (slow-motion) close-up of a splash already in progress: a tilted translucent orange disc (printed star/compass logo) sits against a crushed red Coca‑Cola can, which rests on a pale rounded dome (balloon/stone) at the bottom of frame. A blurred tree trunk and fence form the background. Brown cola and white spray surround the objects.
visible_changes: The orange disc tilts and translates leftward, drifting progressively out of the left edge of the frame by the end of the clip.

The crushed red can rotates in place (its printed barcode/QR label and the concave silver base swing from the upper‑left toward the lower‑left), so the can's orientation changes without a new crush event being shown.

The liquid spray evolves: a brownish burst at the disc's left at the start gives way to a larger whitish mist cloud that expands to the right of and behind the disc, thickens through the middle frames, then breaks into finer droplets.
The pale dome at the bottom and the background tree/fence stay at nearly fixed positions, indicating the apparent motion belongs to the disc/can/spray rather than to camera movement.
The disc's printed logo remains a surface marking (not a separate object or reflection) throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The impact or trigger that launched the disc, can, and splash (the clip opens with the spray already airborne).
What the disc and can do after they exit the left of the frame, and whether they remain in contact or separate.
The full extent and settling of the splash beyond the last frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the disc and can are physically linked or merely coincident in the spray.
Exact nature of the pale dome (balloon, snowball, or stone) and of the liquid (cola vs. mixed fluids).
Whether the slight leftward drift of the whole scene is object translation or a small camera pan; background cues are too blurred to confirm.
